key_doubts.prompt: In the melodic minor scale, the sixth and seventh degrees are raised on the way up and lowered on the way down. Which pattern of whole and half steps represents
verdicts: gemini: wrong (The keyed answer is the major scale pattern; the ascending melodic minor is W-H-W-W-W-W-H.)
sonnet: wrong (Ascending melodic minor is W-H-W-W-W-W-H, which is the second option. The keyed pattern W-W-H-W-W-W-H is not a minor scale.)

key_doubts.prompt: In the standard right‑hand fingering for any major scale, which scale degree is always played by finger 4?
verdicts: gemini: wrong (Finger 4 plays the 7th degree only in sharp scales starting on white keys; in F major it plays degree 4, and in flat scales it falls on other degrees.)
sonnet: wrong (Finger 4 is not always on the 7th degree; in F major it falls on B-flat (4th), and flat-key fingerings differ.)

key_doubts.prompt: When harmonizing a melody with secondary dominants at the Advanced level, the voice‑leading rule for a V⁷/vi resolving to vi requires which interval between the
verdicts: gemini: wrong (The chordal seventh resolves down by step to the third of vi, which is a descending major second (e.g. D to C in C major), not a minor second.)
sonnet: wrong (In V7/vi the seventh (e.g. D in E7) resolves down a major second to the third of vi (C), not a minor second.)
